title: What Shoe Should I Race In?
summary: Whether you’re running a 5K, half-marathon or full 26.2, Nike has an ideal shoe to help you harness speed and confidence and keep you comfortable, supported and propelled forward.
body_markdown:
These days, a never-ending shoe wall can make the process of picking the perfect racing pair feel as daunting as the course you’re prepping for. What should you consider: comfort? Technology? Weight? All of the above?


Enter Emily Farina, Senior Principal Researcher of Running Footwear and Biomechanics at the Nike Sport Research Lab. Farina spends her days developing[the ideal shoes to help runners achieve their goals](https://about.nike.com/en/magazine/a-decade-of-the-super-shoe-how-nike-redefined-speed) . And in her view, picking the best race-day shoe is a balance of knowing what a shoe can do for the course you’re tackling and where you are in your running journey.


A skillfully selected race-day shoe can help you get the most out of the training you’ve put in, whether you’re seeking speed, comfort, limited weight or a combination of all of the above.


While Farina says personal feel is crucial, she also notes that different shoes offer different attributes. See how that breaks down for the 5K, half-marathon and marathon.


What to Wear for a 5K


The gateway distance of the racing world, 5Ks are the most likely to mix running veterans with newbies. When picking your shoe, think about where you fall on that spectrum, says Farina. If you’re experienced and out for pure speed or a new personal best, a shoe’s performance components, like springy foam or even a speedy plate, should be your determining factors. Farina says that’s why the[Nike Vaporfly](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/vaporfly-4-streakfly-2-official-images) — with its light weight, resilient[ZoomX foam](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/collections/explainer-how-nike-s-innovative-foams-deliver-performance-and-comfort) and carbon-fiber plate that provide pop — is finding a home in shorter races.


If it’s your first 3.2, a racing shoe might not be a necessity from a speed or monetary standpoint, despite offering an energetic benefit, says Farina. “Confidence in how you feel and how you are moving is what’s most key for a beginner,” she says, and that can often be found in the same shoe model that you train in. Both the[Vomero Plus](https://www.nike.com/a/vomero-plus-release-info) and[Pegasus Plus 2](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/unlock-race-day-speed-for-everyday-runs-with-nike-new-tempo-trainer-the-pegasus-plus-2) are popular options for everyday runs that can instill confidence, and with ZoomX foam or a Zoom Air unit, they perform well when you push it on race day.


“Beginners benefit from shoes that are comfortable, make running feel easier and providing support as you pound the pavement,” says Farina. In other words, for a runner whose goal is to make it over the finish line, prioritizing what feels good and helpful over what feels speedy can be the best bet.


This logic scales beyond the 5K — if your everyday Vomeros, for example, feel best for your half- or full marathon, prioritizing that comfort and confidence is your move.


> “Beginners benefit from shoes that are comfortable, make running feel easier and providing support as you pound the pavement.”
>
>
> Emily Farina, Senior Principal Researcher of Running Footwear and Biomechanics


For pure speed, its hard to beat the Nike Vaporfly 4, which combines a lightweight upper with a propulsive carbon-fiber plate to help you push further and faster.


If speed is a priority in your everyday shoe and you don't want to jump into a racer, the Nike Pegasus Plus 2, with a Zoom Air unit in the forefoot, is the best of both worlds.


For prioritizing cushioned protection and efficiency, the Nike Vomero Plus is an ideal option, and for any road race distance if you aren't set on a racing model.


What to Wear for a Half-Marathon


Half-marathoners are more likely to have worked through longer runs and are ready to put the trainers away and race in a shoe that can give them an edge. Farina says that means energetic and durable cushioning that continues giving as you hit double-digit mileage, an effective plate for quick turnover when you want it, and a shoe that packs in all that speed-creating technology while staying lightweight.


If you’re newer to the distance, Farina says the[Nike Swooshfly](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-swooshfly-makes-race-day-feel-more-possible) , an inclusive racer, can be a great choice. Engineers created Swooshfly to mimic the performance qualities of the Vaporfly, with a silhouette and ride that’s designed to be more approachable and supportive. Swooshfly features[Nike SkyX](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-swooshfly-makes-race-day-feel-more-possible) , a new beaded foam compound created for long-lasting energy return, a wider platform for fit and feel, and a thinner carbon-fiber plate that still provides a pop experience.


“The Nike Swooshfly could be a great option for first-timers or anyone who’s looking for an entry-level price point in a race-day shoe; it's designed to be more accommodating for support and efficiency versus all-out speed,” says Farina.


> “The Nike Swooshfly could be a great option for first-timers or anyone who’s looking for an entry-level price point in a race-day shoe; it's designed to be more accommodating for support and efficiency versus all-out speed.”
>
>
> Emily Farina


The Nike Swooshfly is a new super shoe designed to deliver the lightweight feel and energy return you want for the half-marathon and marathon, while remaining approachable and accommodating.


Speed is achieved in the Nike Vaporfly 4 with the help of premium, lightweight ZoomX foam.


For those looking to unleash speed on the starting line, Farina says the go-to is the[Vaporfly](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/vaporfly-4-streakfly-2-official-images) . Light, fast and snappy, the Vaporfly was built to achieve speedy times in the 5K, 10K and half-marathon, says Farina, and can give runners an edge in these distances because of its leaner profile.


What’s more, she adds, the Vaporfly can be an excellent supplemental shoe for crossing over to marathon training and logging longer, faster workouts.


What to Wear for a Marathon


As marathon fields grow year over year, so too do the list of shoe features that runners can depend on as they take on the iconic distance. That includes lighter foams that provide high energy return, carbon-fiber plates that guide you over the long haul, and components like Air units that can offer continued cushioning step after step.


In Nike’s lineup, Farina says there’s one shoe that has spent years earning its place as the people’s champ: the Nike Alphafly. The newest Alphafly, the Alphafly 4, has an Atomknit upper for a snug fit and new ZoomX LT foam that delivers 10 percent more energy return than its predecessor while being 5 percent lighter. “With Alphafly 4, we spent years listening to athletes, studying how fatigue impacts performance and running mechanics, refining every element of the system to help runners maintain efficiency when it matters most,” says Farina. “Our goal was simple: Create a shoe that helps athletes feel more confident and capable deep into the race. That’s what Alphafly 4 was built to do.”


Newcomers to the Nike marathon lineup are the Swooshfly and[Nike Apex](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/introducing-nike-apex-the-next-leap-in-marathon-speed) , which service separate ends of the endurance spectrum. As it does in the half-marathon,[the Swooshfly offers a fast, stable ride](https://about.nike.com/en/magazine/how-nike-designed-swooshfly-an-invitation-the-marathon-starting-line) and allows new marathoners to push themselves with confidence. “For marathoners who want to get the efficiency benefits of a racer but with more of your training shoe feel and cost, there’s Swooshfly,” says Farina.


> “With Alphafly 4, we spent years listening to athletes, studying how fatigue impacts performance and running mechanics, refining every element of the system to help runners maintain efficiency when it matters most. Our goal was simple: create a shoe that helps athletes feel more confident and capable deep into the race. That’s what Alphafly 4 was built to do.”
>
>
> Emily Farina


The Nike Apex features a pair of double-stacked Air Zoom units, ZoomX LT foam, and a cutting-edge carbon-fiber plate to help you reach peak performance.


The Nike Alphafly 4 provides support and enegry for the long haul; while it's an ideal marathon shoe, it's also an elite option for the half, especially if energy return is your top priority.


The Swooshfly Flyplate has five layers of carbon fiber, compared to eight layers in the Alphafly 4, to increase flexibility for new marathoners. Its wider platform is meant for stability and support.


Consider Apex the result of what Nike’s designers and sports scientists can produce at their best. It’s the first racing shoe to feature two double-stacked Air Zoom units, located in the forefoot, which helps it deliver up to 40 percent more energy return than the Alphafly 3. While Farina says Apex was made using[insights from elite marathoners](https://about.nike.com/en/magazine/how-nike-created-apex-and-its-next-prototypes-with-elite-athletes) , including seven-star marathoner Eluid Kipchoge, it’s a shoe that has been tested across a range of athletes and speeds, worth the consideration of any marathoner whose goal is to shave every possible second and push their own limits.


Maybe that runner is you.
